## The idea

This project adds the vertical dimension. Choose a short song, hymn, or keyboard
miniature in which melody, bass, and inner harmony can each be followed. Encode
the three roles as independent structures on one shared timeline. The data
should read like a score model: a reader can inspect what each part does and
what sounds at a particular beat without tracing a long chain of `play` and
`sleep` calls. The project builds on the Roman-numeral engine from
[Lesson 28](../06-chords-and-harmony/28-diatonic-chords-roman-numerals.qmd),
voice-leading checks from
[Lesson 31](../06-chords-and-harmony/31-voice-leading-optimisation-problem.qmd),
and independent timelines from
[Lesson 47](../10-texture-and-arrangement/47-independent-voices.qmd).

Meter applies independently to every active voice. The melody can divide four
beats into a pattern unlike the bass, but each must account for the same bar.
Chord labels also need comparison with the notes sounding during their spans.
A passing tone, suspension, or anticipation may lie outside the chord and still
be correct. Preserve the label and explain the melodic or rhythmic function
instead of altering the analysis merely to silence a mismatch report.

Begin with strict alignment and plain synths. At this stage you need to hear
attacks, rests, overlaps, and harmonic clashes without long releases or effects
obscuring their source. Arrangement becomes useful after the score runs from
beginning to end and the structural reports agree with the music.

## Run this

The two-bar model stores melody, bass, and harmony in separate arrays. Global
starts place all three on one coordinate system, threads allow the melodic and
bass timelines to advance independently, and an end-time check confirms that
the roles agree on the length of the passage.

```{.ruby audio=""}
use_bpm 70

melody = [
  {note: :e4, start: 0.0, duration: 2.0},
  {note: :g4, start: 2.0, duration: 2.0},
  {note: :f4, start: 4.0, duration: 2.0},
  {note: :e4, start: 6.0, duration: 2.0}
]

bass = [
  {note: :c2, start: 0.0, duration: 4.0},
  {note: :f2, start: 4.0, duration: 4.0}
]

harmony = [
  {notes: chord(:c3, :major), start: 0.0, duration: 4.0, symbol: :I},
  {notes: chord(:f3, :major), start: 4.0, duration: 4.0, symbol: :IV}
]

define :play_events do |events, synth_name, amp|
  use_synth synth_name
  cursor = 0.0
  events.each do |event|
    sleep event[:start] - cursor
    play event[:note], release: event[:duration] * 0.85, amp: amp
    cursor = event[:start]
  end
end

ends = [
  melody.last[:start] + melody.last[:duration],
  bass.last[:start] + bass.last[:duration],
  harmony.last[:start] + harmony.last[:duration]
]
raise "parts end at different times" unless ends.uniq.length == 1

in_thread { play_events melody, :piano, 0.85 }
in_thread { play_events bass, :fm, 0.5 }

use_synth :hollow
harmony.each do |event|
  play_chord event[:notes], release: event[:duration] * 0.9, amp: 0.35
  sleep event[:duration]
end
```

The melody moves in two-beat values above bass roots and quieter four-beat
triads. It changes more often than the harmony but less often than a walking
line might. All three roles stop after eight beats. Their event counts differ,
yet their final boundary is shared.

## Change one thing

1. Shorten the final melody duration to 1.5. The alignment assertion stops the
   program before playback because the melody now ends at 7.5 beats. If the
   source contains a half-beat of silence, represent that time explicitly
   rather than lengthening the preceding note or weakening the check.
2. Restore the duration and change the first melody note from E4 to F-sharp4.
   Against a C-major I chord, the new pitch produces a conspicuous clash and a
   pitch-class mismatch. Use the source to decide whether pitch, chord label, or
   analysis is wrong; the report alone cannot choose.
3. Restore E4 and move the bass C up one octave. The chord identities and
   durations remain fixed, but the space between bass and harmony narrows.
   Compare the clarity of the inner register before changing any amplitudes.

## Why it works

The shared timeline acts as an interface. Each part owns its events, while all
starts and durations use the same origin and unit. This makes independent
rendering, bar validation, muting, and transposition possible. It also avoids a
fragile design in which the bass's sleeps become the clock for the melody and a
single local edit silently moves every other voice.

Chord checking reduces sounding pitches to pitch classes with `note % 12` and
compares them with the active chord's pitch classes. A mismatch is an invitation
to inspect the beat. Passing tones move between chord members; suspensions hold
an earlier note into a new harmony; anticipations arrive before their chord.
Each can create a deliberate mismatch whose timing explains its role. The
validator should expose such notes, not flatten them into the triad.

Whole-piece alignment is necessary but insufficient. Two voices can end at
beat 32 even if one contains a three-beat bar followed by a five-beat bar.
Partition each role by measure, include rests in the account of elapsed time,
and assert the meter before combining the parts. Local integrity makes the
shared final boundary meaningful.

Once the reports are clean, the structured data supports arrangement without
rewriting the source. Melody, bass, and inner harmony can receive distinct
synths, registers, pans, envelopes, and effect depth. Mute one role during
review to hear what the others contribute. The score remains an authority while
the renderer explores ways of making its roles audible.

## Take it further

Complete a sixteen-to-thirty-two-bar source containing melody and accompaniment.
Deliver separate melody, bass, and harmony structures on one timeline, with
metric checks for every active voice in every bar. Produce a report that
compares each sounding pitch class with the active chord and annotate every
intentional non-chord tone by function. Then arrange the parts so each remains
traceable when all three sound. Melody, bass, and harmony should be independently
mutable or muteable, and no synth, pan, or effect choice should enter the source
score data.
